subject: Patho 1
description: Reversible and irreversible injury, necrosis, apoptosis, adaptations.

questions.text: Which of the following is the earliest reversible change seen in cells exposed to hypoxia?
questions.explanation: Failure of the Na+/K+-ATPase pump from ATP depletion causes influx of Na+ and water, producing cellular swelling (hydropic change), the earliest reversible change. Pyknosis, karyolysis, membrane rupture and mitochondrial amorphous densities occur with irreversible injury.

questions.text: Which finding best indicates that cell injury has become irreversible?
questions.explanation: Irreversibility is marked by inability to restore mitochondrial function (large flocculent amorphous densities) and profound membrane damage. The other changes are reversible.

questions.text: A patient has a myocardial infarction. Which type of necrosis is typically seen in the infarcted myocardium?
questions.explanation: Ischemic infarcts of solid organs (heart, kidney, spleen) show coagulative necrosis, with preserved tissue architecture for some days. The brain is the exception, where infarction produces liquefactive necrosis.

questions.text: Which of the following is the key mediator of the execution phase of apoptosis?
questions.explanation: Executioner caspases (3 and 6) cleave cellular substrates and activate DNases, producing the apoptotic phenotype. Bcl-2 is anti-apoptotic, and RIPK1 is involved in necroptosis.

questions.text: Which adaptation is expected in the uterus during normal pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Pregnancy-related uterine enlargement results from estrogen-driven smooth muscle hypertrophy and hyperplasia.
